cohort: The study included childbirths in South Carolina from 2018 to 2021, specifically focusing on nulliparous, term, singleton, vertex (NTSV) pregnancies (n = 65,974) and those without prior cesarean (primary, n = 167,928).
finding: Black women consistently had higher odds of NTSV cesarean delivery compared to White women, while disparities for primary cesarean deliveries were less pronounced, except for a lower rate among Black women in rural settings during the peri-pandemic period.
